title: Res Gestae Divi Saporis (ŠKZ) — Inscription of Shapur I at the Ka'ba-ye Zartosht, Naqsh-e Rostam
language_note: Trilingual: Middle Persian (Pahlavi, east wall), Parthian (west wall), Greek (south wall). Original composition likely Middle Persian/Parthian; Greek is a contemporary translation carved on the same monument.

original_text_note: Verbatim Parthian recovered 2026-08-09 from Parthian Sources Online, reproducing Huyse 1999 (Corpus Inscriptionum Iranicarum III.I.1); English translation by Jake Nabel. Two chapters are given in both Huyse's transliteration and his transcription: §1 (Shapur's titulature) and §20 (the roll-call of Roman provinces taken — Thrace, Bithynia, Asia, Pamphylia, Isauria, Lycaonia, Galatia, Lycia, Cilicia, Cappadocia, Phrygia, Syria). The site notes that Huyse's text is reproduced there without diacritical marks. The Middle Persian recension is substantially damaged in situ; the Greek recension is separately available via PHI. Chapters 2-19 and 21-51 remain to be pulled if fuller coverage is wanted.
reference_translation: [§1] I, the Mazda-worshipping god Shapur, king of kings of Iran and Not-Iran, whose race is of the gods, son of the Mazda-worshipping god Ardashir, king of kings of Iran, whose race is of the gods, grandson of the god King Pabag, am lord of Iran. [§20] From the land of Thrace, from the land of Bithynia, from the land of Asia, from the land of Pamphylia, from the land of Isauria, from the land of Lyconia, from the land of Galatia, from the land of Lycia, from the land of Cilicia, from the land of Cappadocia, from the land of Phrygia, from the land of Syria.
translation_source: Jake Nabel, Parthian Sources Online, translating the Parthian text of Huyse 1999.
secondary_citation: https://parthiansources.com/texts/skz/ (Parthian original text, transliteration, translation, ed. Huyse 1999)
notes: Hero-tier source for Persia: directly documents Roman emperors (Gordian III, Philip the Arab, Valerian) in a non-Roman, trilingual monumental inscription. Strong candidate for the cross-lingual retrieval demo (Greek vs. Middle Persian/Parthian recensions of the same text).
